entries.reason: REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (was 'unreviewed' since the gate was seeded 2026-09-23). No better mechanism exists today, measured rather than assumed: (1) `uninstall quit:` addresses NSApplications by bundle id, and BOTH helpers are bare binaries, not applications -- `divoomd` carries an embedded `__TEXT,__info_plist` with CFBundleIdentifier com.divoom.divoomd (verified with otool on the shipped Divoom.app), but that plist exists for macOS Bluetooth TCC attribution and does not register the process with LaunchServices, so `quit:` cannot reach it; `divoom-menubar` has no plist section at all. (2) The menubar agent is spawned detached (start_new_session) and orphans to launchd when the GUI quits, so it has no LaunchAgent to unload either. (3) There is no pidfile: the daemon's stable handle is the /tmp/divoom.sock control socket, which carries no process identity. The pattern is as narrow as the need: -f matches the full command line, and the string is the installed app's own helper path, so it cannot match the main app at Contents/MacOS/Divoom; `|| true` makes a no-match a non-failure. The REAL fix needs divoom-control to give the helpers a stable identity -- a LaunchAgent, or a pidfile -- and that is recorded in ROADMAP T2.3.
